items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — he went straight from 'at 11:00 AM, what are we moving?' into pricing with no roadmap or timeframe set.
Never asked 'how are you today?' — no opening pleasantry at all.
Never used the caller's name. Emily gave it in her first sentence ('Hi, my name is Emily') and Sergio did not say it once for the rest of the call.

Customer said 'there's a couple of other things that need to be boxed up just like the smaller things' and packing was never addressed — no packing service quote, no materials pricing, no 'do you want us to pack that or will it be boxed before we arrive?'
Box count never asked, despite the customer raising boxing needs.
No inventory taken at all. He asked twice ('did you want to give me the inventory list or was he gonna give me that') and accepted deferral to a later callback, then booked anyway.
No time range given for the job — 'if you can give me kind of more details of like the inventory list, it'll give me a gauge of how long this would take' and then no gauge was ever provided.
Only asked story count at origin ('is that a single story or two story home?'). Never asked about stairs, floor, or elevator at the destination new build.
Additional rooms never probed — no garage, storage unit, attic, or balcony question on a 4,500 sqft two-story origin.

No special-considerations probe — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns. The caller volunteered that parking is on Oak Crest; Sergio noted it but never asked how far the carry is from that parking to the door.
No moving-stressors question — never asked what she or Taft was worried about.
No 'pricing is super simple' opener; the pricing block ended with 'essentially that's how kind of how it works there?' instead of a clean framing.
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained. 'Insurance' was named only as one item in the included list — the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse coverage and the 60c/lb baseline never came up.
Meet Your Mover never mentioned.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned.

No hidden fees pitch never delivered — no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees. This is a brand differentiator and it was skipped on a call where a $70 trip charge had just been added.
Disassembly / reassembly inclusion never mentioned even though furniture is being moved.
Never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, and never explained 15-minute prorated increments after the 2.5-hour minimum.
No deposit never mentioned — one of the two strongest closing differentiators, on a call that closed a booking.

Save Your Ass speech entirely absent. This was the single best-fit call for it: a partial move of 'smaller things' where consolidating loose items and taking a carload would directly cut billable hours.

Email handoff was thin — he asked 'what's a good email I can send this over to?' but never said what the email contains, never mentioned the bolded detail list at the top, and never asked her or Taft to reply with corrections. On a booking taken third-hand with no inventory, the reply-with-corrections ask is the safety net and it was skipped.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Gave the callback number and 'ask for Sergio' but never gave business hours.
top_strength: Logistics discipline was the best part of this call. Before quoting anything he pulled the zip codes specifically to check exposure ('what's the beginning of the zip code, so I can double-check for any trip fees?'), verified truck availability for 11:00 AM and said out loud he was re-checking so he wouldn't misinform her ('let me double-check so I'm not lining you'), then delivered clean, correct numbers: $95 per mover per hour, $190 for two movers, a 2.5-hour minimum, a $70 trip charge, and a $545 minimum total — which is arithmetically right and quotes the 2.5-hour policy correctly. He also captured the operational detail the caller volunteered (parking on Oak Crest) into the notes, took the end customer's full name spelling, cell, and email, and closed the booking on the call in six minutes.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Sergio quoted and booked a next-day move with no inventory whatsoever, then blocked a full day as a placeholder. He asked for the list twice, got 'I'm gonna have him give you a call,' and let it go. He should have held the scope conversation on the line: 'Emily, I can hold 11:00 for you right now — but before I put a crew on it, walk me through room by room what's leaving the house, even roughly. If it turns out to be more than the coffee table and the rug, I'd be sending the wrong size crew and your bill goes sideways. Can you get Taft on the phone in the next hour, or give me his number and I'll call him myself?' Booking first and estimating later is exactly the pattern behind our estimate-accuracy gap. Second priority: the differentiators are simply missing — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no hidden fees, and no deposit all went unsaid on a call that closed, which means we won a booking on price alone and gave the customer nothing to defend us with. Third, run the Save Your Ass prep speech; on a partial move of 'smaller things' it is the easiest money we leave on the table. LIVE BUSINESS RISKS, in order: (1) a 4,500 sqft two-story origin is over the 1800 sqft virtual-walkthrough threshold and was booked with no walkthrough and no item list — the exemption only holds if it really is a handful of selected items, and the caller explicitly did not know what those items are; (2) the customer said items need to be boxed up and packing was never quoted, so packing hours and materials will appear on the invoice unpriced, which is precisely the surprise-bill scenario our no-hidden-fees promise exists to prevent; (3) Sergio told Emily he would 'plan for the full day right now and then once I get more details from him I can make that adjustment' — if Taft never calls, that adjustment never happens and we run a day-long block against a possible two-hour job; (4) the booking was taken from a third party at a law firm on behalf of Taft Foley with the confirmation going to Taft's email — nobody verified the details with the person actually paying, and no reply-with-corrections ask was made.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient and cooperative but purely transactional — zero name use, no affirmations or empathy markers, and no rapport beyond the task, though the caller stayed positive and closed with 'I appreciate it.'
